content.comment_body: Hello, I'm facing an issue with my setup. I created a program using [product_name] version [version_no] and the simulation works correctly. However, when I connect a [sensor_model] probe, the [product_name] is not registering any readings. Could someone assist me?
What is a [sensor_model] sensor? Do you have a link or a data sheet for this sensor?
It's actually a [sensor_model], a two-wire probe.

Assuming the diagram is correct, the wire marked in yellow should be connected to the M1 wire. Even after connecting M1 to the yellow terminal, nothing changes, and my amplifier still doesn't function.

Your last picture shows an older module. The newer [product_name] analog module has terminals U1-, IC1, U1+, U2-, IC2, U2+. Connect U1- and IC1 to one end of the [sensor_model], and U1+ to the other end. Regards, [user_name]
Why are you asking about a [sensor_model] probe?

I think [sensor_model] is a type of probe. I'm using it for temperature measurements – unless I'm mistaken. One thing is clear: the [product_name] is not identifying it, and monitoring B0031 shows no change in values, whether it's connected or not, even when the temperature varies.
It's connected as you've suggested, but the [product_name] still isn't registering the temperature.

You are using the wrong analog module. Your module only supports 0-10V or 0/4-20mA signals, not for PT1000 sensors. You have an [product_name] module with article number [article_no]; you need an [product_name] RTD module with article number [article_no].
You can find the module type printed on its housing.
Thanks [user_name] for the info. I've now connected the [sensor_model] probe to the [product_name] RTD module as shown, but the issue with reading still persists.
The sensor amplifier still shows negative values indicated by the program, while the actual temperature is 22°C.
Can someone explain how to get the [product_name] to correctly display the AI7 value? Maybe my program is incorrect? Any suggestions for amplifier settings are welcome. Thanks in advance.

It's not difficult! You're likely dealing with a PT 100/1000 sensor, not a [sensor_model]. I didn't see the RUN/STOP LED lit green in your photo. What do you mean by AI7? Is it the operand AI7 or the I7 terminal on the base module? Please clarify for accurate support. Back to the main point. You have a [product_name] 12/24 RCE, specifically [product_name] version [version_no] ([article_no]). Onboard analog inputs AI1 and AI2 are enabled by default on the base module (see File > Properties > Offline settings > I/O settings). First channel on your [product_name] RTD is operand AI3. Amplifier settings after the AI3 channel: For whole numbers: Sensor: PT100/1000 Unit: Celsius Resolution: 1 Decimal places: 0 Display range: -50 to 200°C For one decimal: Sensor: PT100/1000 Unit: Celsius Resolution: 1 Decimal places: 1 Display range: -50.0 to 200.0°C

I'm unsure where my mistake is. This is my first attempt. I followed everything [user_name] advised, but the [product_name] still won't read the PT1000. Quick question: does AI1 correspond to terminal I7?

First, your comment on block B004 is incorrect. The scaling in your situation is -50 to 200°C (whole numbers only). It's hard to say what exactly is wrong as I can't see what you're doing. If your [product_name] RTD module is the first analog input on the right of the base module and onboard analog inputs are set to default (2 enabled), AI3 would be the first channel. Analog input configurations: - 0 enabled: AI1 and AI2 for the first analog module - 2 enabled: AI1 = terminal I7, AI2 = terminal I8 on base; AI3 and AI4 for the first analog module - 4 enabled: AI1 = I7, AI2 = I8, AI3 = I1, AI4 = I2 on base; AI5 and AI6 for first analog module
[Non-English] My problem is likely due to the designation AI3 = I7. What should I connect to I7? Currently, nothing is in terminal I7. Is the PT1000 missing power?
Please use English.
I think there may be some misunderstanding on my part.

Looking at the photos, I see an [product_name] module next to the base module, then a digital module, followed by an analog output module, and finally the [product_name] RTD module. This order is possible, but I recommend placing digital modules first, then analog inputs, then analog outputs, rather than mixing them. However, that's up to you. The analog input numbering depends on how the base module is configured – it could begin with AI1, AI3, or AI5. Try each (AI1, AI3, AI5, AI7) to see which registers your sensor value. Regards, [user_name]
I've changed the order of input and output modules as shown in the photo, but the problem persists. Can you clarify what 'AI3 = I7' means? I have nothing in I7—is this causing my issue?

AI3 does not relate to I7. Now your [product_name] RTD module is the first analog input module. Depending on how the base module's analog inputs are set: - 0 enabled: AI1 is the first channel of [product_name] RTD - 2 enabled: AI3 is the first channel of [product_name] RTD - 4 enabled: AI5 is the first channel

To test which AI channel your PT sensor uses, utilize the display on your [product_name]. Press the cursor down repeatedly to reach the start screen, then press right until you reach screen 3/9 (AIs 1-5). This screen will show which AI registers the PT value. Around 25°C should correspond to roughly 300 units.

That's mistaken: with 0 analog inputs enabled, the [product_name] RTD module begins with AI1; with 2 enabled, it starts with AI3; with 4 enabled, AI5. Try the attached test program—AI1 should display the correct value. If not, check your wiring. Regards, [user_name]
You're correct, I've updated my previous post.

For longer distance sensors, I'd use a PT100/1000 transmitter, which provides a 0/4-20mA output—this can be directly connected to the AM2 module input. There's no need for the RTD module in that case.
But the user already has an [product_name] RTD module.

[Non-English] I also have two modules: AM2 and AM2 RTD. Unfortunately, I lack sufficient expertise to read from PT100 or other 4-20mA sensors. I've loaded the sample program and identified the AI3 terminal, but can't get an accurate reading. Maybe the PT1000 sensors I bought aren't PT1000, but K10, which I can't distinguish. It's odd that temperature changes don't affect the amplifier's Ax value. I also have the two modules: AM2 and RTD type. Sadly, I lack the ability to correctly read the PT100 or any 4-20mA signal. I've tried the suggested program, pinpointed AI3, but can't obtain a valid reading. Maybe the PT1000s I bought are actually something else, but I'm not sure how to identify them. It's strange that changes in temperature don't reflect at the amplifier's output.

If you have a multimeter, measure the resistance of the PT100 or PT1000 without it being connected to the RTD module. PT100 should show 100 Ohms at 0°C, PT1000 1000 Ohms at 0°C. Other thermistor types will have different values. See [url] for more details and example resistance tables for different temperatures. Regards, [user_name]
I want to know: since I can't read values from AI3 and AI4, is my attached program correct or could there be errors affecting the readings from the PT1000 sensor connected to AI3?
I've already posted the correct analog amplifier settings for PT100/PT1000 using the RTD input module in an earlier post.

Upload your program as a ZIP file instead of pictures—it is easier to check that way. Also, after instructions on measuring the PT100/PT1000 with a multimeter, there hasn't been any feedback. If you're still uncertain, respond to the questions or suggestions provided. Regards, [user_name]

Sorry [user_name], I followed your advice and tested the [sensor_model] with a multimeter. After reviewing the table, I confirm that it's an NTC1000 (see photo). I'll send my program zipped soon. I have four temperature readings to measure: AI3 = boiler temp ([sensor_model]) AI4 = hot water temp ([sensor_model]) AI5 = external temp (4-20mA, range: 50 to -200, upper limit 50, lower -50) AI6 = heating delivery temp

If the sensors are NTC type, they're not compatible with [product_name]. You have several options: 1. Buy PT100/PT1000 sensors for the RTD module 2. Purchase an NTC-to-0..10V transmitter, if available, allowing you to connect via the analog module (not RTD module) 3. Get sensors with direct 0..10V or 4..20mA output Transmitters or direct outputs let you optimize the measurement range for your application and improve resolution. PT100/PT1000 sensors range from -50°C to +200°C, but for heating you might only need 0°C to +100°C, or -30°C to +70°C for outdoor use. All analog inputs of [product_name] modules support 1000 steps; narrower ranges offer better resolution (e.g., 0.1°C with analog transmitters, 0.25°C with PT100/PT1000). For testing, you can use a fixed resistor (100 Ohm or 1 kOhm)—the program should display 0°C. You can also use the resistance-temperature table for verification. If you have valid sensors or a resistance-temperature spreadsheet, upload it for reference. Regards, [user_name]

I've ordered a PT100 as suggested. Quick question: I have a probe (see picture) with 4-20mA output, but the analog module isn't reading it—the amplifier always shows the same value. What does 'AIx corresponds to Ix terminals' mean? For example, does AI1 correspond to terminal I7? Do I need to connect anything specific to I7?

To work effectively with [product_name], consult the system manual. It's straightforward to understand the settings for analog inputs. The base module typically has eight digital inputs (I1 to I8). Some versions (e.g., 12/24RCE) let you use four inputs as analog—so I7 is also AI1, I8 is AI2, I1 is AI3, and I2 is AI4. Analog inputs can be configured: - 0 analog inputs: I1-I8 are digital, next analog module starts with AI1 - 2 analog inputs: I7 = AI1, I8 = AI2; next analog module starts with AI3 - 4 analog inputs: I7 = AI1, I8 = AI2, I1 = AI3, I2 = AI4; next analog module starts with AI5 This allows you to connect up to eight PT100/PT1000 or 4-20mA sensors, if you have four expansion modules. The base module must be set to 0 analog inputs for this. For mixed sensors or 0-10V outputs, connect them to the base module (not all base modules offer analog inputs—check the labeling). Your image of the 4-20mA probe needs more detail—please provide a terminal assignment and technical specifications. Share a manufacturer link if possible. Regards, [user_name] P.S. After ordering a PT100 sensor and reading my previous post, you'll understand if it's the best choice.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is attempting to connect a temperature probe to a [company_name] controller using expansion modules. The main challenge is a mismatch between sensor type and module capability; for example, using a module that only reads voltage or current signals with a sensor that outputs resistance, which requires a dedicated RTD module. The discussion highlights the importance of verifying hardware compatibility and correct configuration of analog input channels, as well as the need to use sensors suitable for the input type of the respective module.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the hardware setup to behave like the simulation and display temperature readings from the probe, hoping for simple plug-and-play functionality between sensor and controller module.
